newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 7.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Greece's former king, Constantine, yesterday denied the charges contained in the archives of former president of the republic Constantine Karamanlis that he planned a coup to return to power during the first post-dictatorship government. Constantine counter-charged that Karamanlis had urged him to declare a dictatorship before the 1967 coup and also launched volleys against the present-day leadership of Greece, saying he doubted whether they were able to deal with the country's problems.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis will try to rein in the adverse reactions from a number of ruling party PASOK MPs at today's meeting of the Parliamentary Group but is not expected to directly refer to the letter by 32 MPs expressing reservations about the government's recent moves on Greek-Turkish relations.

--The standing committe on public organisations has recommended major changes to the face of the wider public sector which is expected to radically change the operation and structure of these bodies. The report has been passed on to Interior Minister Alekos Papadopoulos.

--George Rallis, a former prime minister and veteran political figure, yesterday called ex-king Constantine's charges that he joined Karamanlis in calling for a dictatorship "a falsification of history". Karamanlis is expected to respond to the former monarch's claims today.

--Environmental organisation Greenpeace yesterday presented its new electric car - with a speed of up to 70 kph and no fuel emissions it is considered to be the solution to Athens' chronic air pollution.
--The book published by the confidante and head of the former king's private office disproves Constantine's claims yesterday.
--The Social Security Foundation, IKA, has come in for criticism for delaying giving an elderly pensioner the money for reading glasses.
--The ten biggest banks have made profits of 232 billion drachmas in 1996, an increase of 15.0 percent over the previous year's figures.
--There's a storm brewing over the government's plans for the 47 billion drachma budget for the Public Power Company's plant in Florina.
--The Constantine-Karamanlis spat has put the new leader of New Democracy Costas Karamanlis in a difficult position.
